exposure: health seeking behavior (number of antenatal clinics attended)
cohort: The study included 375 postnatal mothers of institutionally delivered newborns.
finding: Early initiation of breastfeeding (39.2%) and exclusive breastfeeding (54%) rates were found to be low, with socio-economic status, mode of delivery, parity, and health-seeking behavior identified as significant determinants.
mod_finding: Mothers who had a normal vaginal delivery were more likely to follow early initiation of breastfeeding (EIBF), while Caesarean delivery was associated with lower rates of exclusive breastfeeding (EBF).
